## Requirements (from the pull request description)

Requirement: Feature request #2297 in MessagePack-CSharp.

Why: Generated code is hard to test. It drags the coverage number down.

Before and after: Before: generated code counts in coverage. After: it is marked `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` and skipped.

Must preserve: Projects that build today must still build. Generated code must work the same.

## The feature request the Requirement row points to (issue #2297, word for word)

# Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A
kept: Before and after (first part: 'Before: generated code counts in coverage. After: it is marked [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] and skipped.')
The feature request #2297 that the Requirement row points to, word for word
leftOut: Summary and tags (they describe the real fix)
Second half of 'Before → after' (it says which projects the real fix leaves out)
Approach (it names the templates and a helper the real fix changes)
Alternatives (it says the real fix added no on/off setting)
given.note: The feature request names the attribute ([ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]) but no file. The author of the real change had the same request.

Generated code is now marked `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. Nothing was built or run (no .NET SDK here), so this is reasoned from the code only.

## How the attribute is applied

- **Formatters** (object, string-key, enum, union): on the generated formatter class itself.
- **Resolvers** (`[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]` and `[CompositeResolver]`): on each generated member (private constructor, `GetFormatter<T>`, `FormatterCache<T>`, the `…GetFormatterHelper` class), not on the `partial class`.

The resolver is a partial class the user can co-author. A class-level attribute would fail with CS0579 for anyone who already applied it, and would silently exclude their own members from coverage.

## Files changed

- **Templates**: the six `.tt` files in [Transforms](src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms) (including [StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt](src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/StringKey/StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt)) emit the attribute.
- **Template code-behind**: the six matching `.cs` files are hand-synced to the `.tt` changes.
- **[TransformUtilities.cs](src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/TransformUtilities.cs)**: doc comment recording that no attributes may go on the nesting partial declarations, and why.
- **Snapshots**: all 225 expected `.g.cs` files under [Resources](tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Resources) updated to the new output.
- **[GenerationTests.cs](tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/GenerationTests.cs)** and **[CompositeResolverGeneratorTests.cs](tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/CompositeResolverGeneratorTests.cs)**: three new tests where the user has already put the attribute on their resolver, composite resolver, or private-member data type. They reuse existing snapshots, so they fail on a duplicate-attribute compile error or any change in output.
- **[README.md](README.md)**: short "Code coverage" section under AOT Code Generation.

## Things to know

- **Hand-edited generated files**: the template `.cs` files are marked auto-generated, but there is no T4 tooling here. Re-run the T4 transform and the `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests` suite before merging; a mismatch would show up as a snapshot diff.
- **Not excluded**: static field initializers generated into a resolver (`Instance`, and the composite resolver's `formatterList`/`resolverList`) still count, because C# cannot attribute a field initializer. Users who want those gone can put the attribute on their resolver class; the README says so.
- **Left alone**: when a formatter is nested in a generic data type with constraints, the string-key template puts the attribute on the same line as the opening `{`. It compiles; I kept the rest of the output byte-identical rather than fix that layout.
- **No opt-out setting**: the issue said one wasn't needed.
